feature: The panel's drop mark only answers for files, and always clears
summary: The red dashed outline around the right hand panel now only appears for a file arriving from outside the app, and it takes itself off within a second whatever ended the drag, including a drag that never tells anything it ended.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next or Current. Nothing to turn on. Open any picture so the layers list has a few rows.

try.do: Drag any layer's colour swatch (Appearance, the Fill square) up over the layers list and hold it there.
Let go of it anywhere, then look at the panel edge: nothing should be marked.
Pick up a layer row and carry it over another row.
Drag a file the app cannot open, a .txt or a .zip, from the Finder over the layers list and hold it.
Let go of it: the red dashes go with it.
Drag a picture over the same spot: a solid accent edge and a drop line saying where it lands.
Drag that .txt over the panel again and press escape, or let go outside the window: the mark goes within a second.

evaluate: Does dragging anything of the app's own over the panel now feel silent, with no red border flashing up at you?
When a file the app cannot use is over the panel, is one red dashed edge around the whole panel the right amount of warning, or is it too loud for a hover?
The mark clears about a second after a drag ends the hard way. Is that fast enough that it never reads as stuck?
A colour dragged over a layer row now shows the no-entry pointer and no panel mark at all. Is silence right there, or should a layer row say something about a colour dropped on it?
rough: Screen Recording was granted, so every shot above is a real capture of the window, not an offscreen render.

What was actually driven, with the probe: a colour swatch over a layer row, a layer row over another row, an unusable file over a layer row and then let go, a picture over the same row, and a file drag abandoned in the air without a word. Saved to Scripts/playtest/panel-mark-walk.json so it stays a regression check.

Two of the things named in the task were NOT driven, because this document had no shelf: a Library tile and a component tile. A saved colour on the shelf carries exactly the payload the Fill swatch does, so it is covered by the colour case. A component tile carries only the app's own component type, which none of the panel's drop targets is registered for, so it cannot reach this code at all.

The hard limit is a second of nothing happening while no mouse button is down. It cannot fire during a real drag, because a drag holds the button down the whole time, but it does mean the very last resort is a second rather than instant.

Found on the way and NOT fixed here: a layer row picked up and then let go somewhere it cannot land is still in the list's hand afterwards. It no longer confuses a file arriving, but a colour dragged over a row after that can still draw a reorder line. Filed as its own task.
